disclaimer: General guidance only. It does not replace trained responders. In any serious emergency call 112 first.
sources: Indian Red Cross Society / IFRC First Aid Guidelines
St John Ambulance first aid guides

medical.title: Medical emergency
steps: Stay calm. Make sure the area is safe for you and the patient.
Call 112 (or 108 for an ambulance) if the person is unresponsive, struggling to breathe, bleeding heavily or in severe pain.
Ask a nearby person to call campus security / the medical room while you stay with the patient.
Do not give food, drink or medicine unless the person is fully awake and it is their own prescribed medicine.
Keep the person comfortable and still. Note symptoms and the time they started to tell the responders.

fire.title: Fire
steps: Raise the alarm: shout 'Fire!' and activate the nearest fire alarm.
Leave the building immediately by the nearest safe exit. Do not use lifts. Do not stop to collect belongings.
Stay low if there is smoke: cleaner air is near the floor. Cover your nose and mouth with a cloth.
Before opening a door, feel it with the back of your hand. If it is hot, do not open it. Use another exit.
Call 101 (fire) or 112 once you are safely outside. Move away from the building and do not go back in.
Only use an extinguisher on a very small fire, if you are trained, and with your back to an exit.
If your clothes catch fire: stop, drop to the ground, cover your face and roll.

accident.title: Accident / injury
steps: Check for danger (traffic, electricity, chemicals) before going close. Do not become a second casualty.
Call 112 or 108 for any serious injury. Send someone to the gate to guide the ambulance.
Do not move an injured person unless there is immediate danger. They may have a neck or back injury.
Control bleeding by pressing firmly on the wound with a clean cloth.
Keep the person warm and talking. Do not give food or drink.
For electric shock: switch off the power at the source first. Never touch the person while they are still in contact.

security.title: Security threat / harassment
steps: Move to a safe, well-lit place with other people (a hostel reception, guard room or classroom).
Call campus security and 112 (police 100, women helpline 1091). Say exactly where you are.
If someone is following you, do not go to your room alone. Head to a crowded place or the security post.
Do not confront an armed or aggressive person. Get away, lock or block doors, and stay quiet if hiding.
Keep your phone location sharing on. Note descriptions, times and any evidence to report later.

natural_disaster.title: Natural disaster
steps: Earthquake: DROP to your hands and knees, take COVER under a sturdy desk, HOLD ON. Stay away from windows. Do not run outside during shaking.
After shaking stops, exit calmly using stairs (no lifts) and gather in an open area away from buildings, poles and trees.
Flood: move to higher ground at once. Do not walk or drive through flowing water. Stay away from electrical equipment.
Storm or lightning: stay indoors away from windows. Avoid open grounds, trees and metal objects.
Follow instructions from campus authorities and call the disaster helpline 1078 or 112 for rescue.

unknown.title: Emergency (type not clear)
steps: Move to a safe place and stay calm.
Call 112 if anyone is in danger. It connects to police, fire and ambulance.
Tell campus security exactly where you are. Your SOS has already been sent with your location.
Use the buttons below to switch to the closest emergency type for guidance.

unresponsive.title: Person is unresponsive or not breathing
steps: Tap their shoulders and shout. If there is no response, call 112 or have someone call and bring an AED if available.
Check for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
If not breathing normally, start CPR: push hard and fast in the centre of the chest, about 100-120 pushes per minute, about 5 cm deep.
If trained, give 2 rescue breaths after every 30 pushes. If not, keep doing chest pushes only.
Continue until help arrives, an AED is ready, or the person starts breathing.

bleeding.title: Severe bleeding
steps: Press firmly and directly on the wound with a clean cloth. Keep pressing.
If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top. Do not remove the first layer.
If it is safe and no fracture is suspected, raise the injured limb.
Call 112 if bleeding is heavy or does not slow after 10 minutes of pressure.

choking.title: Choking
steps: Ask 'Are you choking?' If they can cough, encourage them to keep coughing.
If they cannot cough, speak or breathe: lean them forward and give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.
If still blocked, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts (stand behind, fist above the navel, pull inwards and upwards).
Alternate 5 back blows and 5 thrusts. Call 112. If they become unresponsive, start CPR.

breathing_difficulty.title: Difficulty breathing / asthma
steps: Help the person sit upright and stay calm. Loosen tight clothing.
If they have their own reliever inhaler, help them use it as prescribed.
Open windows for fresh air. Do not lay them flat.
Call 112 if breathing is severe, lips turn blue, or they cannot speak full sentences.

seizure.title: Seizure
steps: Clear the area of hard or sharp objects. Cushion their head.
Do not hold them down. Do not put anything in their mouth.
Note the time. Loosen tight clothing around the neck.
When shaking stops, gently turn them onto their side. Stay with them.
Call 112 if it lasts more than 5 minutes, repeats, or they are injured or not waking up.

allergic_reaction.title: Severe allergic reaction
steps: Call 112 immediately if there is swelling of the face or throat, breathing trouble or dizziness.
If the person has an adrenaline (epinephrine) auto-injector, help them use it right away.
Lay them flat with legs raised unless they are struggling to breathe (then sit upright).
Stay with them until help arrives.

chest_pain.title: Chest pain / possible heart attack
steps: Call 112 immediately. Do not wait to see if it passes.
Help the person sit down and rest in a comfortable position. Keep them calm.
Loosen tight clothing. Do not let them walk around or exert themselves.
Be ready to start CPR if they become unresponsive and stop breathing normally.

burn.title: Burns
steps: Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes.
Remove rings, watches or tight items near the burn before swelling starts.
Cover loosely with a clean non-fluffy material or cling film. Do not use ice, butter or toothpaste.
Call 112 for large burns, burns on the face, hands or genitals, or electrical and chemical burns.

mental_health.title: Someone may be thinking of harming themselves
steps: Stay with the person. Do not leave them alone. Listen calmly without judging.
If there is immediate danger, call 112. Remove access to anything they could use to hurt themselves, if it is safe to do so.
Call Tele-MANAS (14416), a free mental health helpline in India, and contact the campus counsellor or warden.
Stay until trained help arrives.
